title: ICSE CLASS 7 — Chemistry | Rusting Crystallisation
description: Subject-wise test on Rusting Crystallisation (Chemistry) for ICSE CLASS 7. 25Q.
subject: icse7-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of a physical change?

options.text: A new substance with entirely different properties is always formed.
options.explanation: This describes a chemical change, not a physical change.

options.text: It is generally irreversible.
options.explanation: Physical changes can often be reversed, unlike chemical changes.

options.text: Only the physical state or appearance of the substance changes.
options.explanation: This is the defining characteristic of a physical change.

options.text: A significant amount of heat or light is always produced or absorbed.
options.explanation: This is more typical of chemical changes, not physical changes.

questions.explanation: In a physical change, the chemical composition of the substance remains the same; only its physical properties like shape, size, state, or appearance are altered. No new chemical substance is formed.
questions.hint: Physical changes do not alter the chemical identity of a substance.
questions.subject: icse7-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following daily life processes is an example of a chemical change?

options.text: Melting of butter
options.explanation: Melting is a physical change where butter changes from solid to liquid.

options.text: Dissolving salt in water
options.explanation: Dissolving is a physical change as no new substance is formed.

options.text: Burning of a matchstick
options.explanation: Burning involves a chemical reaction producing new substances.

options.text: Breaking a glass bottle
options.explanation: Breaking is a physical change as the glass remains chemically the same.

questions.explanation: Burning a matchstick involves combustion, which produces new substances like ash, carbon dioxide, and smoke, along with heat and light. This is an irreversible process. The other options are physical changes.
questions.hint: Look for processes that produce new substances or involve combustion.
questions.subject: icse7-chemistry

questions.question: For the rusting of iron to occur, which two specific conditions are absolutely necessary?

options.text: Presence of nitrogen and high temperature
options.explanation: Nitrogen and high temperature do not cause rusting.

options.text: Presence of carbon dioxide and sunlight
options.explanation: Carbon dioxide and sunlight are not necessary for rusting.

options.text: Presence of oxygen (from air) and water (moisture)
options.explanation: Oxygen and moisture are essential for rusting to occur.

options.text: Presence of inert gases and low temperature
options.explanation: Inert gases and low temperature do not facilitate rusting.

questions.explanation: Rusting is an oxidation process where iron reacts with oxygen in the presence of water or moisture to form hydrated iron(III) oxide, commonly known as rust. Both air (oxygen) and water are crucial.
questions.hint: Rusting requires oxygen and moisture.
questions.subject: icse7-chemistry

questions.question: The process of obtaining large, pure crystals of a substance from its solution is known as:

options.text: Evaporation
options.explanation: Evaporation removes the solvent but does not necessarily form crystals.

options.text: Condensation
options.explanation: Condensation involves a gas turning into a liquid, not forming crystals.

options.text: Sublimation
options.explanation: Sublimation is the direct change from solid to gas, not forming crystals.

options.text: Crystallization
options.explanation: Crystallization is the correct term for forming pure crystals from a solution.

questions.explanation: Crystallization is a purification technique where a dissolved solid is allowed to form pure crystals from a saturated solution. It is a physical change as no new chemical substance is formed.
questions.hint: This process involves forming solid crystals from a solution.
questions.subject: icse7-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly highlights a key difference between a physical change and a chemical change?

options.text: Physical changes always absorb heat, while chemical changes always release heat.
options.explanation: This is not always true; physical changes can also release heat (e.g., freezing).

options.text: Physical changes are always reversible, while chemical changes are always irreversible.
options.explanation: Some chemical changes can be reversible under specific conditions.

options.text: A chemical change results in the formation of one or more new substances, unlike a physical change.
options.explanation: This is the key difference between physical and chemical changes.

options.text: Physical changes involve changes in chemical bonds, whereas chemical changes do not.
options.explanation: Chemical changes involve breaking and forming new chemical bonds.

questions.explanation: The fundamental difference is the formation of new substances with different chemical properties in a chemical change. While reversibility and energy changes often differ, they are not the sole or most definitive distinguishing features.
questions.hint: Focus on the formation of new substances.
questions.subject: icse7-chemistry

questions.question: Consider the following processes: I. Melting of an ice cube II. Photosynthesis in plants III. Burning of natural gas Which of these processes are examples of endothermic changes (processes that absorb heat)?

options.text: I and II only
options.explanation: Melting ice and photosynthesis are endothermic processes.

options.text: II and III only
options.explanation: Burning natural gas is exothermic, not endothermic.

options.text: I and III only
options.explanation: Burning natural gas is exothermic, not endothermic.

options.text: I, II and III
options.explanation: Burning natural gas is exothermic, not endothermic.

questions.explanation: Melting of an ice cube (I) absorbs heat from the surroundings to change from solid to liquid. Photosynthesis (II) absorbs light energy (a form of heat energy) from the sun to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose. Burning of natural gas (III) is an exothermic process, releasing heat.
questions.hint: Endothermic processes absorb heat, while exothermic processes release heat.
questions.subject: icse7-chemistry

questions.question: To prevent rusting, a common method involves applying a protective layer of zinc metal over iron articles. This process is specifically called:

options.text: Painting
options.explanation: Painting is a preventive measure but not the specific process described.

options.text: Oiling
options.explanation: Oiling is a preventive measure but not the specific process described.

options.text: Galvanization
options.explanation: Galvanization is the correct term for coating iron with zinc.

options.text: Electroplating
options.explanation: Electroplating is a different process and not specifically for rust prevention.

questions.explanation: Galvanization is the specific process of coating iron or steel with a thin layer of zinc to protect it from rusting. Zinc acts as a sacrificial metal, corroding before iron. Painting and oiling are other preventive measures, but not galvanization.
questions.hint: This process involves coating iron with zinc.
questions.subject: icse7-chemistry

questions.question: When a candle burns, the melting of wax is a physical change. Which associated phenomenon represents a chemical change?

options.text: The wax cooling and solidifying.
options.explanation: This is a physical change (solidification).

options.text: The wax vaporizing near the flame.
options.explanation: This is a physical change (vaporization).

options.text: The burning of the wax vapor at the wick.
options.explanation: This is a chemical change (combustion).

options.text: The wax changing its shape.
options.explanation: This is a physical change (change in shape).

questions.explanation: The burning of the wax vapor at the wick is a chemical change (combustion) because it produces new substances like carbon dioxide, water vapor, and soot, along with light and heat. Melting, vaporization, and solidification are physical changes.
questions.hint: Look for the process that involves combustion or produces new substances.
questions.subject: icse7-chemistry

questions.question: Cooking an egg is considered a chemical change because:

options.text: The egg changes its physical state from liquid to solid.
options.explanation: This describes a physical change, not the chemical change.

options.text: The egg absorbs heat from the pan.
options.explanation: Absorbing heat is not the defining factor for a chemical change.

options.text: New chemical bonds are formed and broken, leading to irreversible changes in its proteins.
options.explanation: This is the correct explanation for why cooking an egg is a chemical change.

options.text: The egg becomes hot to touch.
options.explanation: This is a physical change in temperature, not a chemical change.

questions.explanation: Cooking an egg involves the denaturation of proteins (albumen), where the protein molecules undergo significant structural changes due to heat. This forms new substances with different properties (texture, color, smell) and is largely irreversible, hence it's a chemical change.
questions.hint: Consider the changes in the egg's proteins during cooking.
questions.subject: icse7-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following processes does NOT involve the formation of a new substance?

options.text: Souring of milk
options.explanation: Souring of milk involves a chemical change (formation of lactic acid).

options.text: Digestion of food
options.explanation: Digestion involves chemical changes (breaking down food molecules).

options.text: Burning of magnesium ribbon
options.explanation: Burning involves a chemical change (formation of magnesium oxide).

options.text: Boiling of water
options.explanation: Boiling is a physical change where water changes state but remains H₂O.

questions.explanation: Boiling of water is a physical change where liquid water changes into gaseous steam. The chemical composition (H₂O) remains the same. Souring of milk, digestion of food, and burning of magnesium ribbon all involve chemical reactions forming new substances.
questions.hint: Look for processes that do not alter the chemical identity of the substance.
questions.subject: icse7-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of a physical change?

options.text: A new substance with different properties is formed.
options.explanation: This describes a chemical change, not a physical change.

options.text: It is usually irreversible.
options.explanation: Physical changes can often be reversed, unlike chemical changes.

options.text: The chemical composition of the substance changes.
options.explanation: This is a characteristic of a chemical change, not a physical change.

options.text: No new substance is formed, only the form or state changes.
options.explanation: This is the correct definition of a physical change.

questions.explanation: In a physical change, the chemical identity of the substance remains the same; only its physical state or appearance changes.
questions.hint: Physical changes do not alter the chemical composition of a substance.

questions.question: Identify the change that is purely physical from the given options:

options.text: Burning of a magnesium ribbon
options.explanation: Burning is a chemical change as it produces new substances.

options.text: Melting of ice into water
options.explanation: Melting is a physical change as no new substance is formed.

options.text: Rusting of an iron nail
options.explanation: Rusting is a chemical change as it forms a new substance (iron oxide).

options.text: Cooking of food
options.explanation: Cooking involves chemical changes in food.

questions.explanation: Melting of ice is a change of state where water (H₂O) remains water, just in liquid form. The other options involve the formation of new substances.
questions.hint: Look for changes that do not produce new substances.

questions.question: Why is the dissolving of salt in water considered a physical change?

options.text: Because heat is always released during the process.
options.explanation: Heat release is not a defining feature of physical changes.

options.text: Because the salt completely disappears and cannot be recovered.
options.explanation: Salt can be recovered by evaporation, so it does not disappear.

options.text: Because no new chemical substance is formed, and the salt can be recovered by evaporation.
options.explanation: This is the correct explanation for why dissolving salt is a physical change.

options.text: Because it is an irreversible process.
options.explanation: Dissolving salt is reversible by evaporation.

questions.explanation: When salt dissolves, it mixes with water but doesn't chemically react to form a new substance. The salt can be separated from water by physical means like evaporation, indicating it's a physical change.
questions.hint: Consider whether a new substance is formed during the process.
questions.subject: icse7-chemistry

questions.question: For rusting of iron to occur, which two conditions are absolutely essential?

options.text: Presence of carbon dioxide and water
options.explanation: Carbon dioxide is not essential for rusting.

options.text: Presence of oxygen (air) and water (moisture)
options.explanation: Both oxygen and water are essential for rusting to occur.

options.text: Presence of nitrogen and high temperature
options.explanation: Nitrogen and high temperature are not required for rusting.

options.text: Presence of sunlight and dry air
options.explanation: Sunlight and dry air do not promote rusting.

questions.explanation: Rusting is the oxidation of iron, which requires both oxygen (from the air) and water (moisture) to form hydrated iron(III) oxide.
questions.hint: Rusting involves the reaction of iron with oxygen and water.
questions.subject: icse7-chemistry

questions.question: Assertion (A): Burning of a candle is classified as both a physical and a chemical change. Reason (R): The melting of wax is a physical change, while the burning of the wick (producing CO₂ and water vapor) is a chemical change.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The assertion and reason are both correct, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason does correctly explain the assertion.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true.

questions.explanation: The assertion is true because a candle burning involves wax melting (physical change) and the wax vapor reacting with oxygen to produce new substances (chemical change). The reason correctly explains both aspects.
questions.hint: Consider the different processes involved in burning a candle.
questions.subject: icse7-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following processes always results in the formation of one or more new substances?

options.text: Sublimation
options.explanation: Sublimation is a physical change where a substance changes directly from solid to gas.

options.text: Freezing
options.explanation: Freezing is a physical change where a liquid turns into a solid.

options.text: Chemical change
options.explanation: Chemical changes always result in the formation of new substances.

options.text: Condensation
options.explanation: Condensation is a physical change where a gas turns into a liquid.

questions.explanation: The defining characteristic of a chemical change is the formation of new substances with different chemical properties from the original ones. Sublimation, freezing, and condensation are physical changes.
questions.hint: Chemical changes produce new substances, while physical changes do not.
questions.subject: icse7-chemistry

questions.question: Galvanization is a popular method to prevent rusting of iron. This process involves:

options.text: Applying a thick coat of paint on iron articles.
options.explanation: Painting is a method to prevent rusting but not galvanization.

options.text: Coating the iron surface with a layer of zinc.
options.explanation: Galvanization involves coating iron with zinc.

options.text: Mixing iron with carbon to form an alloy.
options.explanation: Mixing iron with carbon forms steel, not galvanization.

options.text: Heating the iron to a very high temperature.
options.explanation: Heating alone does not prevent rusting.

questions.explanation: Galvanization protects iron by coating it with a layer of zinc, which acts as a sacrificial metal and prevents iron from coming into contact with oxygen and water.
questions.hint: Galvanization involves coating iron with a specific metal.
questions.subject: icse7-chemistry

questions.question: The process of obtaining large crystals of a pure substance from its solution is known as:

options.text: Evaporation
options.explanation: Evaporation removes the solvent but does not necessarily form crystals.

options.text: Crystallization
options.explanation: Crystallization is the process of forming crystals from a solution.

options.text: Decantation
options.explanation: Decantation is a method to separate a liquid from a solid by pouring.

options.text: Filtration
options.explanation: Filtration separates solids from liquids using a filter.

questions.explanation: Crystallization is a specific process used to separate pure solid in the form of crystals from a solution. It is a physical change as no new substance is formed.
questions.hint: This process involves forming solid crystals from a solution.
questions.subject: icse7-chemistry

questions.question: A change in which heat energy is released into the surroundings is known as an:

options.text: Endothermic change
options.explanation: Endothermic changes absorb heat energy.

options.text: Exothermic change
options.explanation: Exothermic changes release heat energy into the surroundings.

options.text: Isothermal change
options.explanation: Isothermal changes occur at constant temperature.

options.text: Physical change
options.explanation: Physical changes can be either exothermic or endothermic.

questions.explanation: Exothermic changes are those that release heat energy, often causing the surroundings to warm up. Endothermic changes absorb heat.
questions.hint: Exothermic changes release heat, while endothermic changes absorb heat.
questions.subject: icse7-chemistry

questions.question: When you tear a piece of paper into several smaller pieces, what type of change has occurred?

options.text: A chemical change, because the paper's properties are altered.
options.explanation: Tearing does not alter the chemical properties of the paper.

options.text: A physical change, because no new substance is formed.
options.explanation: Tearing is a physical change as no new substance is formed.

options.text: An irreversible change, as the pieces cannot be put back together perfectly.
options.explanation: Irreversibility does not define a chemical change.

options.text: A change that involves a significant energy release.
options.explanation: Tearing does not necessarily involve significant energy release.

questions.explanation: Tearing paper only changes its size and shape, not its chemical composition. The paper remains paper, so it is a physical change.
questions.hint: Consider whether the chemical composition of the paper changes.

questions.question: Classify the following change: 'Melting of an ice cube into water.'

options.text: Chemical Change
options.explanation: No new substance is formed; only the state changes.

options.text: Irreversible Change
options.explanation: Melting is reversible by freezing the water back into ice.

options.text: Physical Change
options.explanation: The change is in the state of matter, not the chemical composition.

options.text: Both Chemical and Physical Change
options.explanation: Only a physical change occurs here.

questions.explanation: When ice melts, it changes from solid water to liquid water. The chemical composition (H₂O) remains the same. This is a change in state, which is a physical change.
questions.hint: Consider whether the chemical identity of the substance changes.

questions.question: For rusting of iron to occur, which of the following conditions are absolutely essential?

options.text: Only oxygen
options.explanation: Oxygen alone is not sufficient; moisture is also required.

options.text: Only water vapour
options.explanation: Water vapour alone is not sufficient; oxygen is also required.

options.text: Both oxygen and water
options.explanation: Rusting requires both oxygen and water (or moisture).

options.text: High temperature and dry air
options.explanation: High temperature and dry air prevent rusting.

questions.explanation: Rusting is the oxidation of iron in the presence of both oxygen (from air) and water (or moisture). Without both, rusting will not take place.
questions.hint: Think about the environmental factors required for rusting.
questions.subject: icse7-chemistry

questions.question: Which statement is generally true for a chemical change but NOT for a physical change?

options.text: Energy is always absorbed during the process.
options.explanation: Energy absorption or release can occur in both physical and chemical changes.

options.text: The change is easily reversible by simple physical means.
options.explanation: Physical changes are often reversible, but chemical changes are not.

options.text: No new substance is formed, only the state changes.
options.explanation: This describes a physical change, not a chemical change.

options.text: A new substance with entirely different properties is formed.
options.explanation: This is the defining feature of a chemical change.

questions.explanation: The formation of a new substance with different chemical properties is the defining characteristic of a chemical change. Physical changes do not result in new substances.
questions.hint: Consider whether the change results in a new substance.

questions.question: Galvanization is a process used to prevent rusting of iron. Which of the following statements best explains how galvanization protects iron?

options.text: It makes the iron surface shiny and attractive.
options.explanation: This is a superficial benefit, not the primary purpose of galvanization.

options.text: It converts iron into a less reactive metal, preventing oxidation.
options.explanation: Galvanization does not convert iron into a less reactive metal.

options.text: It coats the iron with a layer of zinc, which acts as a barrier and is more reactive than iron.
options.explanation: Zinc provides both a physical barrier and sacrificial protection.

options.text: It removes all oxygen molecules from the surface of the iron permanently.
options.explanation: Galvanization does not remove oxygen permanently; it prevents oxygen from reaching the iron.

questions.explanation: Galvanization involves coating iron with a layer of zinc. Zinc acts as a protective barrier, preventing direct contact of iron with oxygen and water. Additionally, zinc is more reactive than iron, so if the coating is scratched, zinc corrodes preferentially (sacrificial protection), saving the iron underneath.
questions.hint: Consider the role of zinc in protecting iron from rusting.
